errors.why: This is the commentator's abbreviation formula 'apply [the sutra text] likewise', marking an elided stretch of the quoted sutra, not a statement that something was composed.

note: Faithful rendering of the Sadaprarudita episode quoted from the sutra; only the commentarial abbreviation formula is misread.

errors.english: if its essence and the ascertainment of originating from it follow after it
errors.why: It is indicativeness (go bar byed pa nyid) that follows the ascertainment of tadātmya and tadutpatti, not the ascertainment that follows it; the next sentence ('if it does not follow the ascertainment but still has it as its reason') is likewise inverted as 'is still the reason for it'.
The gloss says the root's 'it is likewise' is 'not a refutation' (i.e. it concedes rather than denies), not that the refutation consists of the words 'it is not'.

note: Dense Pramāṇa commentary rendered word-for-word; the direction of the dependence between indicativeness and its ground, and the closing gloss, are muddled, and ldan pa can (saṃyogin) as 'the possessor' obscures the term.

errors.english: Through that, i.e., through its nature, how could one logically deduce, "If it changes from a specific nature, why would this also not change?" It is not logical to deduce that entities are possessed of a person's desire.
errors.why: The Tibetan says that against things governed by their nature it IS reasonable to press the consequence 'as it arises from a specific nature, why not here too?', whereas things dependent on a person's wish cannot reasonably be subjected to such a consequence.

fix.find: Through that, i.e., through its nature, how could one logically deduce, "If it changes from a specific nature, why would this also not change?" It is not logical to deduce that entities are possessed of a person's desire.
fix.replace: Through that, i.e., through their nature, it is reasonable to press the consequence, "Just as it arises from a specific nature, why would it not arise here too?"; but entities that depend on a person's wish cannot reasonably be subjected to such a consequence.

errors.english: Having made such an assertion, it is because of intending it in that way.
errors.why: brda byed pa is the convention-maker (the author of the mantra, cf. previous side), whose intention determines that the result accrues to some and not others; the English loses this agent.

note: Generally follows the argument about mantra efficacy, but the key contrast between natural causation and will-dependent things is turned into its opposite.

errors.english: [note: referring to a traditional example of something that is not fire, such as a cold or divine object]
errors.why: śakramūrdhan ('Indra's head') is the standard name for an anthill, from which a smoke-like vapour rises; it is not a cold or divine object.

fix.find: [note: referring to a traditional example of something that is not fire, such as a cold or divine object]
fix.replace: [note: śakramūrdhan, 'Indra's head', the standard name for an anthill, from which a smoke-like vapour rises]

errors.english: fire does not transcend being a benefactor [note: a cause] and performing the act of benefiting [note: producing an effect]
errors.why: phan gdags bya / 'dogs byed is the pair upakārya-upakāraka, 'the benefited and the benefactor', i.e. the relation of effect and cause, not two aspects of being a benefactor.

note: The argument about fire, smoke and their specific natures is broadly followed, but the śakramūrdhan note is wrong and the upakārya-upakāraka pair is misrendered.

errors.why: dmigs kyis bsal ba here means singling out / specification (nirdhāraṇa): 'among those' singles out cetanā from the pair, it does not exclude it.

note: A sound rendering of Avalokitavrata on MMK 17.2-3 (cetanā and cetayitvā karma); only the 'specification' sense of 'among those' is misread as exclusion.
Faithful rendering of the general and specific (figurative and direct) characteristics of the four truths and the two kinds of seekers of liberation.

errors.english: It is certainly established that the third sign [note: the third characteristic of a logical reason: the absence of the reason in the heterologue or "non-concordant class"] must be known.
errors.why: The word continues tshul from the previous side: tshul gsum pa'i rtags, 'the reason with three modes (trairūpya)', is established as known; it is not 'the third sign', and the note on the third mode is consequently wrong.

fix.find: It is certainly established that the third sign [note: the third characteristic of a logical reason: the absence of the reason in the heterologue or "non-concordant class"] must be known.
fix.replace: It is indeed established that the reason with the three modes (trairūpya) is known.

errors.english: there must be a valid means of cognition (pramana) that establishes the connection between the concordant class and the non-concordant class
errors.why: The pramāṇa establishes the relation (sambandha) between reason and probandum, and it is through it that presence in the sapakṣa and absence in the vipakṣa are established; it is not a connection between the two classes.

note: The discussion of why 'certainty' is specified in the definition of the reason is mostly followed, but the opening misreads the triple-mode reason and the conclusion misattaches what the pramāṇa establishes.

errors.english: much like a person who is the object of desire
errors.why: In context (dream persons, previous side) this is the person imagined or intended (in a dream), not a person who is the object of desire.

errors.english: That is not the nature of reality itself.
errors.why: The root verse says that those who do not see the supreme are not knowers of reality (cf. later mchog mthong ba ma yin pas de nyid rig pa ma yin), not that 'that is not the nature of reality'.

errors.english: whose nature is free from the characteristics of the objects of reality
errors.why: 'Free from characteristics' qualifies the object of reality, toward which the Buddhas are equanimous, not the Buddhas' nature.

note: The Yogācāra argument on the Buddhas' elephant gaze is broadly there, but the root verse and several attachments are misconstrued.

errors.english: perfectly knows the causes and the conditions for change
errors.why: The phrase completes 'rnam par dag par' from the previous side: the causes and conditions of beings becoming purified, not of 'change'.

note: A faithful rendering of the sutra passage on the causes of affliction and purification and the Tathāgata's samādhis, apart from the opening phrase that crosses the boundary.

errors.english: for one consumed by desires, there is no satisfaction in wealth
errors.why: In a series contrasting the greedy with the generous, kāmakāma here is one who desires (to fulfil others') wishes, who has no regard for wealth; the English makes him a lustful person never sated (the Sanskrit-side rendering 'no restraint regarding wealth' has the same problem).

note: The bilingual verses (Sanskrit transliteration and Tibetan) are both rendered accurately, the woodcutter and mango images included; one line about wealth is misread.
